clue.text: Sort of English channel

definitions.meaning: ... English is the accent of London and the Thames ... area, a recognised variety of English speech
a broad tidal river mouth forms a channel out to the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of English channel' looks like one phrase about the sea between England and France; it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal river mouth is a wide water channel, and the same name labels a southern English accent.

clue.text: Island qualified to be written up

indicators.note: in a down clue written up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: able means qualified or competent

explanation.surface: An island is qualified to have a write-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Proposition in article more dubious

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: dubious suggests the letters of more are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A proposal contained in an article seems more doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical proposition to be proved.

clue.text: Head off opening move offering scope

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a gambit is an opening move, especially in chess

explanation.surface: Forestalling an opening move gives room for manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means the range or extent of something, its scope.

clue.text: Unscrupulously sensational editor changed with age?

parts.note: yellow journalism is the sensational, unscrupulous kind

explanation.surface: A ruthless tabloid editor has been changed by age.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper and teeth discolour with time, turning yellowish as they grow old.

clue.text: They are expected to point streets out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of streets are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is expected to point out the streets, like a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: SETTERS are gundogs trained to point at game; 'out' rearranges STREETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are gundogs bred to stand pointing at hidden game birds.

clue.text: The most roguish styles are fashionable

indicators.note: fashionable read as fashioned anew, so the letters of styles are reshaped

explanation.surface: The naughtiest styles are in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means mischievous or roguish, so the superlative is the most roguish.

clue.text: It is reasonable to bypass old city in the heat

indicators.note: to bypass means to go round and leave out, so the city is dropped

parts.note: temperature is the degree of heat
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: It makes sense to avoid an ancient city in hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate and restrained, so reasonable.

clue.text: Trying to copy bird with insect — failing finally

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: failing finally means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: Some bird tries to imitate an insect, but fails at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulous means eager to emulate, keen to imitate or rival someone.

clue.text: Artist of the Highland region

definitions.meaning: Graham ... was a twentieth-century English painter
a former county in the far north of the Scottish Highlands

explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' is a link; the clue reads as one painter of Highland scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the English painter Graham Sutherland and to a northern Scottish area.

clue.text: Upfront increase affecting pub regulars?

parts.note: reads like a price rise charged in advance at the pub, but means a swelling at the front of the body caused by too much drinking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Upfront increase' sounds financial; it is a literal growth of the stomach in heavy drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch built up by drinking ale is a front-facing bodily increase common among habitual pub drinkers.

clue.text: Stage horse

definitions.meaning: a stage or platform that something is set on, as a slide or gem is set on a backing
a horse ridden by someone is their steed

explanation.definitionFit: A mount is both a backing or platform for display and an animal to ride, such as a horse.

clue.text: It turns up in one's English trousers perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something pokes up from a pair of English trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ONES with E and TROUSERS; the turned-up nose 'turns up' itself, a nod to trouser turn-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrousse nose is a snub nose whose tip turns upward.

clue.text: Cites vital order for full-time officers

indicators.note: order means putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone quotes the vital rules for regular officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The active list is the roster of officers serving full time in the armed forces.

clue.text: Field did cool

definitions.meaning: John Field, the Irish composer of nocturnes, wrote music: what he did was write it
cool in the sense of calm and unruffled

explanation.walkthrough: Field looks like a meadow or sporting field; it is John Field, the early Romantic composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music, so Field's work is described by the past tense of that verb; it also means calm.

clue.text: Say what you think and get the better of strike

parts.note: to outwit someone is to get the better of them
hit means strike

explanation.surface: Speak your mind and beat a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone to speak up and say what they mean.

clue.text: Good luck gift for abandoned boy

definitions.meaning: a ... or handsel is a gift given for good luck at a new beginning, such as a New Year
the brother of Gretel in the fairy tale, left in the forest by his parents

explanation.definitionFit: The old word for a good-luck present matches the name of the fairy-tale boy left in the woods.

clue.text: Records showing discharge with skin disease

parts.note: an arc is an electrical discharge
hives is an itchy skin rash, urticaria

explanation.surface: Medical records show a discharge with a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' looks medical; it is an electric arc.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are stored historical records, or the place they are kept.

clue.text: Stimulate understanding verbally

indicators.note: verbally means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: understanding means insight, a perceptive grasp

explanation.surface: Someone is spurred on by understanding words.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or provoke someone is to stimulate them into action.

clue.text: Pointed snippet

definitions.meaning: pointed in the sense of sharp and hurtful, as a remark
a clipping cut from a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A wounding remark is sharp-edged, and a press clipping is a small cut-out piece.

clue.text: Sort of Well! of a philosopher caught out

indicators.note: out says the letter for caught is left out of the word

parts.note: Cartesian means of or relating to Descartes, the philosopher
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A philosopher has been caught out over some kind of exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well!' in italics looks like an interjection; it is a water well.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is a type of bore where water rises under its own pressure.

clue.text: Disinclination to move one with detached retina

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: detached suggests the retina's letters coming loose and rearranging

explanation.surface: A patient with a detached retina is reluctant to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency to stay at rest, unwillingness to move.

clue.text: Painful sort of elbow — out of game

definitions.meaning: ... elbow is a painful strained condition of the elbow
a racket sport played over a net

explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is a link: the painful elbow comes out of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport gives its name to a painful elbow strain caused by playing it.

clue.text: Punches champ so, absorbing a lot?

definitions.text: Punches champ so, absorbing a lot?

parts.words: Punches champ so, absorbing a lot?
parts.note: Punches here are Suffolk Punch draught horses champing their feed; to take in as much as they do is to have a huge appetite

explanation.walkthrough: 'Punches' and 'champ' suggest a boxing champion soaking up blows; the Suffolk Punch is an English breed of heavy draught horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who consumes enormous quantities of food, as heavy horses do.

clue.text: Fellow filling the part of Baron Corvo

indicators.note: filling means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: An actor takes on the part of Baron Corvo.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Rolfe was the English writer who styled himself Baron Corvo.

clue.text: . Youthful beauty escaping from the beast

indicators.note: escaping from means the answer lies within the words and gets out of them

explanation.surface: A young beauty flees a monster, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth; the stray dot before the clue is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods.

clue.text: Where is pupil seated? Horse, or sort of bull

parts.note: the pupil of the eye sits in the middle of the iris
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A question about where a schoolchild sits, then a horse or bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild but is part of the eye. An Irish bull is a ludicrously self-contradictory statement.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish bull is a comically illogical statement, so the adjective names that kind of bull.

clue.text: Unusual contents of epistle in ' short story

parts.note: novel means new and unusual

indicators.note: contents of means the inside only, dropping the outer letters of the word

parts.note: an epistle is a letter

explanation.surface: An odd letter is included in a short story.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel or long short story, a piece of short fiction.

clue.text: Put back in earth mature flowers

indicators.note: put with in tells us to place one piece inside another
in, completing put, places one piece inside the other
back says the word for earth is read in reverse

parts.note: a sett is a badger's earth, its burrow
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: Someone replants mature flowers in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' and 'in' together make the container signal, split by 'back', which reverses only the earth. A badger's burrow is called its earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagetes is the genus of marigolds, so the word names these flowers.

clue.text: Cross reference to a leak

definitions.meaning: a cross reference in a book tells the reader to ... so-and-so
a slow leak of liquid through a crack or porous material

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross reference' read as two words is the instruction 'see page'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid oozing slowly out through gaps is a leak of fluid.
